Federal University of Minas Gerais, Brazil (dos Santos, Costa, Montandon, Valente); Federal Institute of Minas Gerais, Brazil (Silva). Funding: FAPEMIG, CNPq

Main: proposes an evaluation method (catalog of six configuration smells for AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, derived from a grey literature review of 14 documents and PR analysis, plus automated detection heuristics). Secondary: evaluates (prevalence and co-occurrence of the smells in 100 popular open-source repositories)
Agent configuration (context) files AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, no version; consumed by Claude Code (CLAUDE.md), Codex, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI (AGENTS.md). No SDD framework

One Markdown file at the repository root (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md; one may just point to the other) with project instructions: setup/build/test commands, architecture, code style, workflow, testing, domain knowledge. Automatic: line-count threshold >=200 lines (Context Bloat); single commit (Init Fossilization); one LLM prompt per smell (gemini-3.1-flash-lite, temperature 0; template Fig. 4, examples for Blind References and Conflicting Instructions) for Skill Leakage, Lint Leakage, Blind References, Conflicting Instructions; Apriori (support 0.05). Manual: every LLM-flagged instance reviewed by the first author; grey literature annotation by first author, checked by second (4 disagreements resolved); grouping and naming by first and last authors; manual PR inspection

N/A for configurations. Findings: 91 of 100 files have at least one smell (9 smell-free). Detected / false positives / precision (Table II): Context Bloat 42 / - / -; Skill Leakage 35 / 6 / 82%; Lint Leakage 62 / 4 / 93%; Blind Reference 16 / 2 / 87%; Init Fossilization 24 / - / -; Conflicting Instructions 28 / 12 / 57%. Leaked skills: testing 10, workflow 8, scaffolding 4, infrastructure 4, architecture 3. Association rules (support / confidence / lift): CI+SL->CB 0.06/0.83/1.81; IF+SL->LL 0.06/0.83/1.31; CI->CB 0.14/0.81/1.76; SL->LL 0.24/0.76/1.19; CB+SL->LL 0.10/0.75/1.18; CI+LL->CB 0.07/0.67/1.44. Most frequent combination CB+LL (12 files). No init-fossilized project dormant. No significance tests

N/A for configurations. Detector precision 57% (Conflicting Instructions) to 93% (Lint Leakage); recall not measured; threshold heuristics not validated. PR analysis added no new smells (2 of 17 PRs discussed smells already found). Limitations stated: annotation bias (sanity check), Google search coverage (keyword trials), LLM non-determinism and model updates (temperature 0, manual check)
Threats: manual annotation bias, Google search may miss documents, LLM-based detection non-deterministic and model-dependent. Future: tools and techniques to detect and prevent configuration smells

Tables II and IV jumbled by pdftotext; values rebuilt from the column order and the text (Section VI-VII). Inconsistencies: text says Skill Leakage 29 of 35 confirmed '(86%)', Table II 82% (29/35 = 82.9%); abstract prevalence ('Lint Leakage ... 62% of the files') and '207 instances' use detected counts including false positives (confirmed total would be 183); intro says two smells 'increase the likelihood of Context Bloat by 83%' while 0.83 is the rule confidence; summary on p. 8 assigns lifts 1.81 and 1.76 loosely ('respectively'). Effect of smells on agent behaviour is assumed, not measured. The grey literature review describes its search (Google, query Fig. 3, top 30, five exclusion criteria, author reputation check) but is a method step, so Q1-Q13 used, not DARE. Replication package: Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.20600327. No pre-registration. Programming language: N/A (multi-language repositories)
